transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I guess… I’ve been getting pulled off task really easily lately. For maybe the past year, small stuff—my phone buzzing, someone walking by my office, even just a random thought—can throw me off before I really catch it. It’s been hard to ignore.
Did you have trouble paying attention as a child?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, looking back, teachers were always moving my seat around because I’d talk too much, get up without asking, or blurt something out before they even finished asking. I didn’t really think much of it then.
Are these attention problems causing difficulties at work?

Yeah… a bit. I’m still getting my work done, mostly, but people are starting to get frustrated. Like in meetings or when I’m supposed to be mentoring someone, things don’t always go smoothly, and I can tell it’s wearing on their patience. It’s also started to affect plans at home, which… isn’t great.
Do you find yourself worrying a lot, even when there isn’t a clear reason to?
Not really, no. I mean, I get stressed about things that are actually happening, but I wouldn’t say I’m worrying for no reason.
Have you been feeling down or depressed lately?
Not really. I mean, I get frustrated sometimes, but I wouldn’t say I’ve been depressed.
Before these attention problems got worse, did you have any head injury or concussion?
Not that I can think of. I don’t remember having a concussion or anything like that before this got worse.
Did these concentration problems get noticeably worse after a specific stressful life event?
Yeah… I guess it did. It’s been harder to manage for maybe a little over a year now—about a year and two months. Around when the conflict with my in-laws started taking up more of our family life.
Since the conflict with your in-laws began, have you been feeling unusually tense or on edge because of it?
I don’t know… maybe a little tense at times, but I wouldn’t say unusually on edge. It’s just been stressful.
Has the conflict with your in-laws made it harder for you to function day to day?

Some, yeah. I’m still keeping up overall, but… it’s started to wear on things. At home there’s less trust when plans don’t go right, and at work people are getting less patient when meetings or mentoring conversations don’t go the way they should.
Compared with what most people would feel in that situation, does your stress about the conflict with your in-laws feel stronger than it should?
I’m not sure. I mean, it feels stressful, but I don’t know if it’s more than what most people would feel. I try not to think about it that way.
Before the conflict with your in-laws started, were these attention and impulsivity problems already causing noticeable trouble in your daily life?

Yeah… I mean, they were there before. I was still getting by, but it was already causing some friction. Like at home, people trusting me less when plans fell apart, and at work people getting impatient if meetings or mentoring talks didn’t go smoothly.
